architecture.mechanism: In-situ/local administration of the active remedy directly at the target site to stimulate a restorative response and “reprogram” the malfunctioning element, instead of relying on centrally delivered systemic supply.
architecture.intervention: For the 2021 Ford Mustang under NHTSA Campaign 23V727000, stop depending on the backordered OEM replacement part and instead remediate at the point of service: reprogram or locally reconfigure the affected electrical/battery module in the vehicle (dealer-level reflash or on-site repair), or fabricate the required repair component locally, so the recall can be completed without the constrained part.
architecture.expected_effect: Recall completion rate rises because remediation no longer waits on the unavailable part; affected vehicles reach Campaign 23V727000 compliance at the service site, cutting customer wait time and closing the unverified-risk gap.
architecture.falsification_test: Apply the in-situ repair (module reprogram or locally fabricated component) to a sample of affected 2021 Mustangs, then verify each vehicle against the 23V727000 acceptance criteria and track recurrence for a set mileage interval; if the in-situ remediation fails compliance or recurs at a higher rate than OEM-part replacement, the mechanism is falsified.
